sections.h2: Where is Beverly and what is it like?
sections.html:
Beverly is a city on the Massachusetts North Shore in Essex County, about 17 miles northeast of Boston. It covers 22.6 square miles, and roughly a third of that is water.

Manchester-by-the-Sea borders Beverly on the east, Wenham on the north, Danvers on the west and Salem on the south. The Danvers River and Beverly Harbor separate Beverly from Salem, and three bridges connect the two cities. The city also includes two small islands, Great Misery and Little Misery, plus a large part of Wenham Lake and a city forest.

The western half of Beverly is more built up. The eastern half, roughly from Woodbury Point eastward, is more rural. The areas residents name most often are:

  • Ryal Side
  • North Beverly
  • Centerville
  • Cove
  • Montserrat
  • Beverly Farms and Prides Crossing

The 2020 census counted 42,670 residents and 17,887 housing units, of which 4.9 percent were vacant. About 31.7 percent of households were one person living alone.

sections.h2: How did Beverly become the city it is today?
sections.html:
English colonists under Roger Conant settled the area in 1626, and Beverly was set off from Salem and incorporated as a town in 1668. It became a city in 1894.

Beverly had the first cotton mill in America in 1787. In 1902 the United Shoe Machinery Corporation began building a quarter mile of reinforced concrete factory buildings, which went into production in 1906 and closed in 1987. Cummings Properties bought the complex in 1996 and turned it into a campus of offices, medical practices, shops and restaurants. Parker Brothers, the game maker, was once headquartered in Beverly too.

President William Howard Taft rented a summer White House in Beverly in 1909 and 1910 and a different house in 1911 and 1912. The city's Beverly Farms section is the reason Beverly Hills, California, has its name.

Beverly's major employers include Axcelis Technologies, Beverly Hospital (part of Lahey), Endicott College and the YMCA of the North Shore. The city is also home to Montserrat College of Art.

Beverly has five public elementary schools for kindergarten through grade 4: Ayers Ryal Side, Centerville, Cove, Hannah and North Beverly. Beverly Middle School serves grades 5 through 8 and opened in 2018, and Beverly High School serves grades 9 through 12. The high school was founded in 1858.

Those employers and campuses sit in different parts of the city, so the address of your house relative to them matters more than the city name alone.

sections.h2: What places draw people to Beverly?
sections.html:
Lynch Park and its beaches in the Cove section are the city's main public park and a popular summer spot for swimming and kayaking. Beverly has five beaches in all, and two yacht clubs, Jubilee Yacht Club in Beverly Harbor and Bass Haven Yacht Club on the Bass River.

Downtown has two historic theaters. The Cabot opened in the 1920s era of movie palaces and reopened as a nonprofit performing arts center in 2014. The Larcom Theatre dates to 1912 and seats 560. The Beverly Cotton Manufactory site in North Beverly marks the first cotton mill in America.

Beverly also calls itself the birthplace of America's Navy because the schooner USS Hannah sailed from Beverly Harbor on September 5, 1775, though Marblehead disputes the claim.

sections.h2: What does North Shore weather mean for a Beverly house?
sections.html:
Beverly has an oceanic climate that borders on humid continental. NOAA normals for the city show about 48 inches of precipitation a year and about 51 inches of snow.

MeasureBeverly figure
Average annual precipitation48.02 inches
Average annual snowfall51.4 inches
Snowiest monthsJanuary and February, about 16 inches each
Record high98 degrees F, most recently June 24, 2025
Record lowMinus 13 degrees F on February 4, 2023

Thunderstorms, tropical rainstorms in summer, and nor'easters in the cooler months are all part of the pattern. Houses near the harbor, the Bass River or the coves are more exposed to that weather than houses inland.

sections.h2: How do roads, rail and bridges affect Beverly sellers?
sections.html:
Route 128 crosses Beverly from east to west and connects to Interstate 95 and Route 1 in Peabody. Route 1A runs north and south through downtown. Routes 22, 62, 97 and 127 end in the city.

Beverly sits where the Newburyport and Rockport lines of the MBTA Commuter Rail split, and it has more commuter rail stations than any municipality in the state except Boston, according to Wikipedia's profile of the city. Stations include:

  • Beverly Depot, near downtown, served by both lines
  • North Beverly, on the Newburyport line
  • Montserrat and Beverly Farms, on the Rockport line

Service to Prides Crossing station is suspended indefinitely. Beverly Municipal Airport sits partly inside Danvers.

One local item stands out. The Hall-Whitaker Bridge over the Bass River on Bridge Street was closed to vehicles by MassDOT in June 2023, with a permanent replacement expected in 2027. Buyers who drive past it daily may ask about it, and a house near that stretch is a fair thing to mention honestly.

sections.h2: What are Beverly's property tax rates and who sets values?
sections.html:
The Beverly Assessors set values for 13,037 real estate parcels and 1,551 personal property accounts as of January 1 each year. For fiscal 2026 the city's residential tax rate is $10.81 per $1,000 of assessed value, and the commercial rate is $20.98.

On a house assessed at $700,000, that rate works out to about $7,567 for the year before any exemption. That is arithmetic on the posted rate, not a quote for your bill, so use your actual bill.

The assessing office also reviews building permits to see how they change a property's value, which means a renovation can raise the next assessment. City Hall is at 191 Cabot Street, and the assessor's line is 978-605-2307. The office posts a fiscal 2026 abatement application, exemption guides for veterans, seniors and others, and a deferral application.

If you want to contest an assessment, the state's Appellate Tax Board guide says the abatement application must reach the assessors by the due date of the first actual tax bill. In quarterly billing towns that is generally February 1. Ask the Beverly collector which schedule applies to you.

sections.h2: What does the closing process look like for a Beverly sale?
sections.html:
Beverly is served by the Southern Essex District Registry of Deeds, and a deed is recorded there at closing. Ask the registry or your closing attorney for the current excise tax and recording fees, because the registry sets its own fee schedule.

  • Smoke and carbon monoxide certificate. Massachusetts requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department for a sale. Call as soon as you have a closing date, and expect an inspection fee.
  • Septic, if any. The eastern part of Beverly is more rural. If your house has a septic system, Title 5 calls for an inspection within two years before the sale, or within six months after if weather prevents it.
  • Attorney. A court decision cited by the Trial Court Law Libraries holds that lender side closings need an attorney's substantive participation.

Most Massachusetts property is recorded land, filed at the Registry of Deeds. A minority is registered land, which has a Land Court certificate of title.

sections.h2: What do Beverly sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Beverly is a coastal city with a large share of its land in the water and a long list of named areas, so two houses a few miles apart can sell very differently.

If you are weighing a listing against a direct sale, ask the assessors for the recent sales list they post and compare. We buy Beverly houses as they are, and you can compare our number with a listing price before you decide.

faqs.q: What county is Beverly, MA in?
faqs.a: Essex County. Beverly is a North Shore city about 17 miles northeast of Boston, and its deeds are recorded at the Southern Essex District Registry of Deeds.

faqs.q: What is the property tax rate in Beverly?
faqs.a: For fiscal 2026 the residential rate is $10.81 per $1,000 of assessed value and the commercial rate is $20.98, according to the Beverly assessors. Rates are reset each fiscal year.

faqs.q: How many neighborhoods does Beverly have?
faqs.a: Wikipedia lists Ryal Side, North Beverly, Centerville, Cove, Montserrat, Beverly Farms and Prides Crossing. These are named areas rather than legal districts.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke detector certificate to sell in Beverly?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet sale requirements. The department charges a fee.

faqs.q: Is the Hall-Whitaker Bridge in Beverly open?
faqs.a: It was closed to vehicles by MassDOT in June 2023, and a permanent replacement was expected in 2027. Confirm current status with the city or MassDOT.
